subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should memory embeddings inherit the selected configured provider’s exact-origin private-network trust when `request.allowPrivateNetwork` is omitted, matching the shared provider transport resolver?
rationale: The patch is mechanically focused, but the default trust behavior for a configured private endpoint is a durable SSRF and compatibility policy choice rather than a defect that an automated repair can safely decide.

options.title: Approve shared-resolver inheritance
options.body: Accept exact configured-origin trust for memory embeddings so they match other provider HTTP requests, retaining explicit `true` for broader private-network access.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep memory embeddings blocked unless `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` is set, then adjust the shared-policy integration and documentation to make that stricter behavior explicit.

options.title: Pause for policy design
options.body: Hold the PR until providers/security owners define one cross-surface contract for configured private endpoints and remote overrides.

recommendation.title: Approve shared-resolver inheritance
recommendation.body: Accept exact configured-origin trust for memory embeddings so they match other provider HTTP requests, retaining explicit `true` for broader private-network access.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review explicitly routes the remaining question to a provider/security owner, but no attributable owner history could be read in this environment.
